newsitem.title: USA: Sated US refiners in no rush to buy foreign crude.
newsitem.headline: Sated US refiners in no rush to buy foreign crude.

text.p: U.S. refiners, faced with full storage tanks and plenty of crude choices, seemed in no hurry to snap up foreign barrels on Thursday, traders said.
North Sea benchmark Brent was on offer around 70 cents under West Texas Intermediate/Cushing for first-half July delivery.
A narrow transatlantic arbitrage kept Brent offers limited and relatively pricey, traders said.
Dated Brent traded at a steady July Brent minus 48 cents a barrel for June 12-14 loading, even with Wednesday's level.
Meanwhile, a trading house was heard to be moving a distressed Saharan Blend cargo from Algeria out of the Gulf area after failing to entice a U.S. buyer.
The last unsuccessful bid heard was around $1.25 under WTI/Cushing, traders said.
Elsewhere, two Colombian Cusiana cargoes changed hands on Wednesday. A June 30-July 1 cargo traded at WTI/Cushing minus $1.42, while a July 6-10 moved at a $1.39 discount.
From Venezuela, the last confirmed deal for Mesa-30 grade was around WTI/Cushing minus $3.25 a barrel. Traders said the price was likely to drift weaker on pressure from a new wave of Iraqi barrels.

Iraq's ambassador to United Nations Nizar Hamdoon told Reuters on Thursday that term contracts held by oil companies from the first round of Iraq's oil-for-food deal would be extended under the renewed accord.
It was yet to be determined, however, whether any of the term deals would be icnreased, or if any new companies might get term contracts, he said.
--Patricia Garip-Bertuol, Patrick Connole NY Energy Desk ((+1 212 859 1620))
